what: Tools for Writing and Manipulating netCDF Files
title: Tools for Manipulating netCDF Files
text: R package, nctools, provides helper functions creating, editing, subsetting, concatenating, transforming netCDF files within R. main entry point write_ncdf(), offers quick convenient way write array data generated R netCDF files minimal boilerplate. core, nctools designed make easy write array data R netCDF files, inspect manipulate files lightweight helper functions. Built around ncdf4, package also includes utilities inspecting variables dimensions, reading writing attributes, renaming variables dimensions, subsetting variables dimension values, concatenating records along unlimited dimensions, changing longitude conventions, applying summary functions selected margins. package especially useful modelling environmental workflows arrays first generated processed R need exported netCDF format storage, exchange, downstream analysis. See https://roliveros-ramos.github.io/nctools/ documentation examples.

title: Locate the depth where a variable reaches a given value — nc_loc
code: local({   input = system.file("extdata",     "temperature_profile.nc",     package = "nctools",     mustWork = TRUE)   output = tempfile(fileext = ".nc")   on.exit(unlink(output))   # Locate the 20 degree isotherm using linear interpolation in depth   nc_loc(input, "temperature", MARGIN = "depth", loc = 20, output = output)   nc = ncdf4::nc_open(output)   result = tryCatch({     list(lon = ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon"),          lat = ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat"),          depth = ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "depth"))   }, finally = ncdf4::nc_close(nc))    # The input profiles follow T(z) = 8 + (surface - 8) * exp(-z / scale)   surface = outer(result$lon, result$lat, function(x, y)     24 + 3 * exp(-((x + 72)^2 / 16 + (y + 15)^2 / 36)) + (y + 25) / 19)   scale = outer(result$lon, result$lat, function(x, y)     50 + 25 * ((x + 80) / 15 + (y + 25) / 19))   analytical = scale * log((surface - 8) / (20 - 8))   analytical[1:2, 1:2] = NA_real_   # Interpolation on 10 m depth intervals approximates the exact solution   error = result$depth - analytical   print(range(error, na.rm = TRUE)) # signed interpolation error in metres   print(max(abs(error), na.rm = TRUE))    image(result$lon, result$lat, result$depth,     xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",     main = "Depth of the 20 degree isotherm (m)")   contour(result$lon, result$lat, analytical, add = TRUE)   # Contours show the analytical depth; the missing corner remains blank }) #> [1] 0.001400802 0.234022209 #> [1] 0.2340222

title: Write data to a netCDF file — write_ncdf
code: local({   # Synthetic daily temperature for January 2001, as in the bundled data   lon = seq(-80, -65, length.out = 15)   lat = seq(-25, -6, length.out = 20)   days = 0:30   spatial = outer(lon, lat, function(x, y)     16 + 6 * exp(-((x + 72)^2 / 16 + (y + 15)^2 / 36)) - 0.15 * (y + 15))   temperature = outer(spatial, days, function(field, day)     field + 2 * sin(2 * pi * day / 365) + 0.2 * sin(2 * pi * day / 7))   temperature[1:2, 1:2, ] = NA_real_    files = vapply(seq_len(3), function(i) tempfile(fileext = ".nc"), "")   on.exit(unlink(files))    # Quick defaults: dimensions are named dim1, dim2, dim3, with index values   write_ncdf(temperature, filename = files[1], varid = "temperature")    # Supply geographic coordinates, time coordinates, and variable metadata   coordinates = list(lon = lon, lat = lat, time = days)   coordinate_units = c("degrees_east", "degrees_north", "days since 2001-01-01")   write_ncdf(temperature, filename = files[2], varid = "temperature",     dim = coordinates, dim.units = coordinate_units,     longname = "Synthetic daily temperature", units = "degree_C")    # Add descriptive attributes, unlimited time, and explicit storage settings   write_ncdf(temperature, filename = files[3], varid = "temperature",     dim = coordinates, dim.units = coordinate_units,     dim.longname = c("Longitude", "Latitude", "Time"),     longname = "Synthetic daily temperature", units = "degree_C",     unlim = "time", prec = "float", missval = -9999,     compression = 4, force_v4 = TRUE,     global = list(       title = "Synthetic temperature for January 2001",       source = "Spatial gradient and Gaussian centre with annual and weekly cycles",       comment = "Synthetic data, not observations; a fixed corner patch is missing."     ))    nc = ncdf4::nc_open(files[3])   tryCatch({     print(ncvar_dim(nc, "temperature"))     print(ncdf4::ncatt_get(nc, 0, "title"))   }, finally = ncdf4::nc_close(nc)) }) #> [1] "lon"  "lat"  "time" #> $hasatt #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $value #> [1] "Synthetic temperature for January 2001" #>
